answer: Each agent’s identity is anchored to a cryptographic vertex derived from a unique quartz‑seeded proof‑of‑work that must be refreshed every epoch. When a new identity appears, the network issues a per‑identity challenge that requires the holder to generate a fresh reasoning trace on a random harbor‑selected data subset, consuming a predictable amount of GPU cycles. An attacker must therefore spend full model compute for every Sybil node, scaling linearly with the number of fake IDs and quickly outweighing any profit.
